title: Here in Thy Temple, Lord, We Meet
description: Here in Thy Temple, Lord, We Meet in Tonic Solfa to ST ANNE, doh is C: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Sebastian Streeter wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 869 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “Humiliation and Prayer”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to ST ANNE; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Here in thy tem-ple, Lord, we meet, And bow be-fore thy throne; A-based and guilt-y, at thy feet We seek thy grace a-lone.

lines: Here in thy temple, Lord, we meet,
Abased and guilty, at thy feet
Our sins rise up in dread array,
And fill our hearts with fear;
O, send thy pity from on high
Bring now thy gracious spirit nigh,
We humbly mourn our follies past,
Resolved, while feeble life shall last,
To tread those paths no more.

licence: Public domain: Sebastian Streeter died in 1867.
credits: Words by Sebastian Streeter (1783–1867), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to ST ANNE by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
